title: SMILE: Smooth Motion for Improved Long-Horizon VLA Execution
comment: Submitted to IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (RA-L)
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models reduce inference cost by executing multiple actions per call, but longer horizons often degrade accuracy because raw chunks contain jitter and outliers. We introduce SMILE, an architecture-preserving interface that predicts B-spline coefficients and decodes them into smooth action sequences. SMILE changes only the action representation, enabling longer fixed horizons while retaining each baseline's backbone and model scale. We apply SMILE to SmolVLA, Evo1, VPP, and DAWN, improving accuracy and amortized inference efficiency across LIBERO, CALVIN, and real-world experiments. SMILE-Evo1 reaches 98.0% with a 1.1x speedup on LIBERO, while SMILE-VPP reaches an average length of 4.42 with a 1.5x speedup on CALVIN. At a matched execution horizon of 10, SMILE-SmolVLA reduces non-boundary acceleration by 78.6% and velocity sign-change rate by 42.3%. Real-world xArm tests show higher success, fewer drops, and fewer contacts. These results establish smooth coefficient-space generation as a route to accurate, efficient long-horizon VLA execution. AI.problem: 论文针对Vision-Language-Action (VLA)模型的长视界（long-horizon）执行问题。VLA模型通过单次调用执行多个动作来降低推理成本，但更长执行视界会导致精度下降，其根本原因是原始动作块（raw chunks）中包含抖动（jitter）和异常值（outliers）。论文试图解决的关键问题是如何在保持现有VLA模型架构和规模不变的前提下，实现更长固定视界下既准确又高效的执行。
AI.method: SMILE是一种保持架构不变的接口（architecture-preserving interface），其技术路线是直接预测B样条（B-spline）系数，并将这些系数解码为平滑的动作序列。SMILE仅改变动作表征（action representation），而不改动各基线模型的骨干网络和模型规模，从而支持更长的固定视界。论文将SMILE应用于SmolVLA、Evo1、VPP和DAWN四个基线模型。
AI.experiment: 摘要给出了多个实验设置与指标：（1）在LIBERO基准上，SMILE-Evo1达到98.0%精度并获1.1x加速；（2）在CALVIN基准上，SMILE-VPP达到平均长度为4.42并获1.5x加速；（3）在匹配执行视界为10的条件下，SMILE-SmolVLA将非边界加速度（non-boundary acceleration）降低78.6%，速度符号变化率（velocity sign-change rate）降低42.3%；（4）真实世界xArm实验显示更高的成功率、更少的掉落和更少的接触。此外，SMILE在LIBERO、CALVIN和真实实验中对四个基线（SmolVLA、Evo1、VPP、DAWN）均提升了精度和摊薄推理效率（amortized inference efficiency）。
